label: Well-Adjusted Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They demonstrate strong psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions, with anxiety scores near floor level and depression and loneliness scores well below typical thresholds of concern.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.79), suggesting robust social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.28), well below clinical concern thresholds
Near-zero anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.04), indicating very low generalized anxiety
Moderate and controlled screen/internet use of 1–3 hours per day
Higher educational attainment suggesting access to cognitive and social resources
tone: Stable, emotionally grounded, and psychologically resilient

label: High-Distress Digitally Immersed Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores (mean 1.72), PHQ-9 depression scores (mean 1.73), and GAD-7 anxiety scores (mean 2.14) are all in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress. With 181 respondents in this cluster, the profile represents a substantial subgroup characterized by compounded emotional difficulties alongside heavy digital engagement.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale (mean 1.72)
Endorses elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9 (mean 1.73)
Shows the highest anxiety symptom levels among profiles on the GAD-7 (mean 2.14)
Engages in prolonged daily digital use exceeding 5 hours
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggests interconnected distress rather than isolated symptoms
tone: Emotionally burdened and persistently distressed, reflecting a convergence of loneliness, depressive mood, and anxious apprehension

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging approximately 1.25, PHQ-9 depression scores around 0.81, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near 0.84, these individuals fall well below clinical thresholds across all three psychological distress measures, indicating generally positive mental well-being.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of loneliness or social isolation
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology, well below clinical concern
Demonstrates low anxiety levels consistent with healthy psychological functioning
Maintains moderate and limited daily screen or internet use (1–3 hours)
Highly educated, suggesting access to cognitive and social resources
